note: EAU prostate 2026. This document could not be routed until stage 1 repaired its heading hierarchy: 343 of its passages arrived carrying a deep subsection with no chapter above it, because the markdown's `#` level saturates at three while EAU's numbering runs to seven. With the hierarchy restored, every rule below matches a chapter title rather than a bare number -- `6.4` as a substring also matches `6.6.4`, and the number alone cannot be trusted.

default.note: EAU numbers every section, so a passage reaching the default sits under a heading that names no clinical situation -- a technique, a complication, a method. That is routing debt to work down with more rules, not a licence to read the body text, which is how v4.0 came to route a passage about diabetes and metformin as locally advanced disease.

rules.note: 118 passages -- a fifth of the document. Written as prose rather than as the numbered tables the split stage recognises by shape, so nothing else catches them. Corpus v4.0 excluded 179 bibliography passages this same way, by the section heading.
The contents pages, and the two stray chapter headings that precede them carrying page numbers -- `7. FOLLOW-UP 151` -- which are contents entries the converter promoted to headings.
A contents entry the converter promoted to a chapter heading, page number and all. It appears before chapter 1 in the file. Excluded here so the real chapter 7 rule claims only the real chapter.
The same, for chapter 8. Without it the chapter-8 rule matches two places and the audit refuses it -- correctly, since one of them is a line from the contents.
Screening addresses men without a diagnosis. Offering it to a patient already staged is the failure a separate setting exists to prevent.
PSA, MRI and biomarkers as applied before a diagnosis exists.
Biopsy reporting applies at every stage. Stated, rather than left to the default, because `spans_settings` is admitted by retrieval and `not_determinable` is not.
The chapter covers low and selected intermediate risk together and does not separate them, so neither is claimed.

Management of high-risk localised disease. v4.0 routed 6.3.3.a and 6.3.3.b to intermediate risk because their prose mentions intermediate risk, inside a chapter whose title says high. The chapter wins.
cN1 M0 specifically. MUST precede 6.3.4, the wider locally-advanced chapter that contains it.
Persistent PSA after radical prostatectomy. v4.0 sent most of this chapter to intermediate risk on the strength of its prose.

Non-metastatic castration-resistant disease, and now routed to it. Until 24 August the vocabulary had no value for this, so the rule recorded what could be said -- non-metastatic, risk not narrowed -- and lost `castration-resistant`; corpus v3 made the same substitution. `prostate_nonmetastatic_castration_resistant` was added later that day for AUA's advanced prostate guideline, and this rule was not revisited at the time. Found by a check for rules whose match sets overlap. MUST precede 6.7, whose rule routes castration-resistant disease to the metastatic setting.

How a treatment is delivered -- surgical technique, radiotherapy dose, complications -- rather than who should receive it. It applies wherever the modality is indicated. Stated rather than left to the default because `spans_settings` is admitted by retrieval and `not_determinable` is not: leaving these on the default makes 100+ passages about operative technique unreachable by every question.
The drugs themselves. Which patient receives them is decided in 6.3, 6.6 and 6.7, each of which has its own rule.
Quality-of-life outcomes are reported across stages. Placed after the exclusion rules so the stray contents entry carrying a page number is excluded rather than routed here.
